Of course, I'd be happy to explain classical conditioning using simple terms that should be understandable regardless of the primary language. Classical conditioning is a learning process that occurs when two stimuli are consistently paired. Initially, one stimulus (unconditioned stimulus, or US) triggers an automatic response (unconditioned response, or UR). Over time, a second, neutral stimulus (conditioned stimulus, or CS) is paired with the US. After repeated pairings, the CS triggers a response (conditioned response, or CR) that resembles the UR, even when the US is not present.

In answer to your question, let me give an example. Imagine a baby (initially) crying (UR) when they are hungry (US). After repeated pairings of crying (CS) with hunger (US), the baby may start to cry (CR) even when they are not hungry, simply because they associate crying with the need to eat. This is classical conditioning.
